segments.en: I really am trying, but I don't have the willpower to just quit.
segments.zh: 我真的在努力，但我没有足够的意志力一下子戒掉。

segments.en: I can't fight with the urge to reach for my pack of smokes in the morning with coffee or after lunch.
segments.zh: 早上喝咖啡时或午饭后，我总忍不住想掏出烟来抽。

segments.en: Please understand.
segments.zh: 请理解。

segments.en: Katerina Fine.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜：好吧。

segments.en: I want a divorce.
segments.zh: 我想离婚。

segments.en: And we are back.
segments.zh: 而我们又回来了。

segments.en: So we have a great part of our show where we like to talk about some phrases that help you attain fluency.
segments.zh: 因此，我们在节目中有很大一部分我们喜欢谈论一些有助于您流利的短语。

segments.en: That means sounding like a native speaker of English.
segments.zh: 这意味着听起来像以英语为母语的人。

segments.en: And today's phrases are wonderful.
segments.zh: 今天的短语很精彩。

segments.en: Enrique Alright, so let's take a look at them now in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: Enrique 好吧，我们现在就在流利表达里看看它们。

segments.en: Fluency Builder Enrique So on Fluency Builder today, let's take a look at two different phrases.
segments.zh: 流利表达Enrique 今天在流利表达环节，我们来看看两个不同的短语。

segments.en: And let's start with the first one.
segments.zh: 让我们从第一个开始。

segments.en: She mentioned something about going cold turkey overnight.
segments.zh: 她提到了一夜之间 cold turkey 戒掉的事。

segments.en: What is that phrase?
segments.zh: 这句话是什么？

segments.en: Cold turkey?
segments.zh: Cold turkey？

segments.en: Katerina Now this is a very strange phrase.
segments.zh: Katerina 现在这是一个非常奇怪的短语。

segments.en: So first of all, why would a turkey be cold?
segments.zh: 首先，为什么火鸡会冷？

segments.en: They have lots of feathers.
segments.zh: 他们有很多羽毛。

segments.en: And second of all, what does it have to do with cigarettes?
segments.zh: 其次，它与香烟有什么关系？

segments.en: Enrique Right.
segments.zh: 恩里克对。

segments.en: So if I say I'm going cold turkey, what is that?
segments.zh: 所以如果我说 I'm going cold turkey，那是什么意思？

segments.en: Katerina So just take this as a phrase.
segments.zh: Katerina 所以把它当作一个短语。

segments.en: Don't think about the actual words because they won't make sense in this context.
segments.zh: 不要考虑实际的单词，因为它们在这种情况下是没有意义的。

segments.en: What we're talking about is quitting smoking entirely.
segments.zh: 我们正在谈论的是完全戒烟。

segments.en: You're not going to cut down.
segments.zh: 你不会削减的。

segments.en: It means today I'm not going to smoke at all and I'm never going to smoke again.
segments.zh: 这意味着今天我根本不会吸烟，我再也不会吸烟了。

segments.en: That means never ever will I smoke another cigarette.
segments.zh: 这意味着我永远不会再抽一支烟。

segments.en: So it's cold turkey.
segments.zh: 所以就是 cold turkey。

segments.en: Enrique So if I go cold turkey, it means I stop doing something immediately and suddenly and forever.
segments.zh: Enrique 所以如果我 go cold turkey，意思是我立即、突然、永远地停止做某事。

segments.en: Katerina Entirely.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜完全。

segments.en: Enrique Alright.
segments.zh: 恩里克好吧。

segments.en: Katerina You can use this phrase for different habits, different things that you do like drinking, for example, or cutting down on sugar.
segments.zh: Katerina 您可以将这句话用于不同的习惯、不同的事情，例如喝酒或减少糖分。

segments.en: But generally we just say this about cigarettes.
segments.zh: 但一般来说，我们只是说香烟。

segments.en: Enrique So it's mostly related to smoking.
segments.zh: 恩里克，所以它主要与吸烟有关。

segments.en: Going cold turkey.
segments.zh: Cold turkey 戒烟。

segments.en: Katerina Some people like to smoke less, like one cigarette a day or one cigarette a week.
segments.zh: Katerina 有些人喜欢少吸烟，比如一天一支烟或每周一支烟。

segments.en: But going cold turkey is supposed to be the hardest.
segments.zh: 但 cold turkey 据说是最难的。

segments.en: Enrique Right.
segments.zh: 恩里克对。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Going cold turkey.
segments.zh: Cold turkey 戒烟。

segments.en: Alright.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: And well, he was explaining the different negative aspects of smoking.
segments.zh: 好吧，他正在解释吸烟的不同负面方面。

segments.en: He said, well, you know, they spend a fortune on cigarettes every month.
segments.zh: 他说，嗯，你知道，他们每个月都在香烟上花一大笔钱。

segments.en: And he said, laws are cracking down.
segments.zh: 他说，法律正在打击。

segments.en: So if the laws are cracking down, what is he trying to say there?
segments.zh: 那么，法律 cracking down，他想表达的是什么？

segments.en: Katerina Well, this is actually a very interesting point because in America right now, it's very hard to smoke in public places.
segments.zh: Katerina 好吧，这实际上是一个非常有趣的点，因为在美国，在公共场所很难吸烟。

segments.en: So this means that the government is trying to stop people from smoking.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着政府正试图阻止人们吸烟。

segments.en: So they say, no more smoking in public places, no more smoking in restaurants, no more smoking in bars.
segments.zh: 所以他们说，在公共场所不再吸烟，不再在餐馆吸烟，不再在酒吧吸烟。

segments.en: And so this means they're cracking down.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着他们正在打击。

segments.en: They're making it harder to do something.
segments.zh: 他们让做某事变得更加困难。

segments.en: Enrique So they are becoming more strict.
segments.zh: 恩里克，所以他们变得越来越严格。

segments.en: I think for this phrase, we should listen to a couple of more examples just to make sure we understand it.
segments.zh: 我认为对于这句话，我们应该再听几个例子，以确保我们理解它。

segments.en: Katerina Example one.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜示例一。

segments.en: Enrique The police are cracking down on drunk driving in our city.
segments.zh: 恩里克 警方正在打击我们城市的酒后驾车。

segments.en: Katerina Example two.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜示例二。

segments.en: Enrique Our school has really started to crack down on tardiness.
segments.zh: 恩里克 我们学校真的开始打击迟到。

segments.en: Katerina Example three.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜示例三。

segments.en: Enrique The president has passed a law that will crack down possession of illegal substances.
segments.zh: 恩里克 总统通过了一项法律，将禁止持有非法物质。

segments.en: Enrique Alright, so the government is cracking down.
segments.zh: 恩里克 好吧，所以政府正在打击。

segments.en: Laws are cracking down.
segments.zh: 法律正在收紧。

segments.en: Katerina Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜 是的，没错。

segments.en: So this is an important one because you read this in the newspapers as well about certain laws and police action.
segments.zh: 所以这很重要，因为你在报纸上也读到过这篇关于某些法律和警察行动的文章。

segments.en: Enrique Alright, great.
segments.zh: 恩里克 好吧，太好了。

segments.en: So I think it's time for us to listen to this dialogue for one last time and then we'll come back and talk a little bit more about this vice.
segments.zh: 所以我认为是时候让我们最后一次听这个对话了，然后我们会回来多谈谈这个恶习。

segments.en: Katerina Ah, it smells like an ashtray in here.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜啊，这里闻起来像烟灰缸。

segments.en: Enrique I know, I know.
segments.zh: 恩里克 我知道，我知道。

segments.en: I really am trying but I don't have the willpower to just quit.
segments.zh: 我真的在努力，但我没有放弃的意志力。

segments.en: I can't fight with the urge to reach for my pack of smokes in the morning with coffee or after lunch.
segments.zh: 早上喝咖啡时或午饭后，我总忍不住想掏出烟来抽。

segments.en: Please understand.
segments.zh: 请理解。

segments.en: Katerina Fine, I want a divorce.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜 好吧，我想离婚。

segments.en: So do you have a problem with this vice as you call it?
segments.zh: 那么你所说的这种恶习有问题吗？

segments.en: Are you a smoker?
segments.zh: 你是吸烟者吗？

segments.en: Enrique I'm really not.
segments.zh: 恩里克我真的不是。

segments.en: I'm the type of person that could maybe smoke socially like if we go out to a bar with drinks, a social smoker like they call it, right?
segments.zh: 我是那种可能会在社交上吸烟的人，就像我们去酒吧喝酒一样，一个像他们所说的社交吸烟者，对吧？

segments.en: Katerina Yeah, I'm jealous.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜 是的，我很嫉妒。

segments.en: Enrique But not really.
segments.zh: 恩里克，但不是真的。

segments.en: You're a habitual smoker, right?
segments.zh: 你是个习惯性吸烟者，对吧？

segments.en: Katerina Right.
segments.zh: Katerina，对。

segments.en: Well, I was.
segments.zh: 嗯，我是。

segments.en: I'm trying to cut down.
segments.zh: 我正在努力减少。

segments.en: So as a habitual smoker, I often smoked every day.
segments.zh: 所以作为一个习惯性的吸烟者，我每天都经常吸烟。

segments.en: Sometimes I smoked a lot and sometimes I smoked less.
segments.zh: 有时我抽了很多烟，有时我抽的少。

segments.en: But right now I'm in a period where I'm mostly quit.
segments.zh: 但现在这段时间我基本上戒了。

segments.en: Enrique Okay, almost.
segments.zh: 恩里克 好吧，几乎。

segments.en: Katerina Yeah, well, I haven't smoked in a while.
segments.zh: Katerina 是的，好吧，我有一段时间没抽烟了。

segments.en: And when I do, it's just one cigarette.
segments.zh: 当我这样做时，它只是一支烟。

segments.en: Enrique Now, it is interesting because like we mentioned, laws are cracking down on where you can smoke.
segments.zh: Enrique 现在，这很有趣，因为就像我们提到的，法律正在打击你可以在哪里吸烟。

segments.en: But also taxes and cigarettes are becoming much more expensive, right?
segments.zh: 但税收和香烟也变得更加昂贵，对吧？

segments.en: Katerina Absolutely, especially where I'm from in Chicago.
segments.zh: 绝对是卡特琳娜，尤其是我来自芝加哥的地方。

segments.en: It's easy to spend maybe 10 US dollars or 12 US dollars on one pack of cigarettes.
segments.zh: 在一包香烟上花费大概 10 美元或 12 美元是很容易的。

segments.en: Enrique On a pack of cigarettes.
segments.zh: 一包香烟上的恩里克。

segments.en: Imagine that.
segments.zh: 想象一下。

segments.en: So then you have people that can't help smoking one or two packs a day.
segments.zh: 所以你有一些人每天都忍不住吸一两包。

segments.en: So how much is that a month?
segments.zh: 那么一个月多少钱？

segments.en: It's just an amazing amount of money.
segments.zh: 这只是一个惊人的金额。

segments.en: Katerina Thousands of dollars.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜数千美元。

segments.en: Well, and I have to say, though, a lot of my friends who used to smoke in America have quit.
segments.zh: 不过，我不得不说，我的很多曾经在美国吸烟的朋友都戒烟了。

segments.en: So this is maybe working.
segments.zh: 所以这可能是有效的。

segments.en: Enrique The whole thing of making cigarettes more expensive.
segments.zh: Enrique 让香烟更昂贵的整个事情。

segments.en: Katerina Yeah, making them much more expensive.
segments.zh: Katerina 是的，使它们变得更加昂贵。

segments.en: Enrique Now, another interesting thing, and what I was reading recently, is that you know those warnings that come on cigarette packs that say smoking kales, smoking causes cancer.
segments.zh: Enrique 还有个有意思的事，是我最近读到的，你知道烟盒上那些警告，写着吸烟致命、吸烟致癌。

segments.en: Actually a study has proven that it's not effective, that people don't mind it or even worry about the cautions on the cigarette packages.
segments.zh: 实际上，一项研究证明它无效，人们不介意，甚至不担心香烟包装上的注意事项。

segments.en: Katerina Well, as a smoker, I could say that, yeah, you generally, if you're going to smoke a cigarette, don't look at the label that much.
segments.zh: Katerina 好吧，作为一个吸烟者，我可以说，是的，你一般来说，如果你要抽烟，不要看太多标签。

segments.en: You just, you know, you throw it in your bag and you forget about it.
segments.zh: 你只是，你知道，你把它扔进你的包里，你就忘记了它。

segments.en: Enrique But it's actually gotten to the point where people choose the cigarette pack based on the picture.
segments.zh: 恩里克，但它实际上已经到了人们根据图片选择香烟包的地步。

segments.en: So it's like, oh yeah, give me the one with the black lungs or give me that one.
segments.zh: 所以就像，哦，是的，给我一个黑肺的，或者给我那个。

segments.en: Katerina Oh, God.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜 哦，上帝。

segments.en: Enrique Yeah, it's interesting.
segments.zh: 恩里克 是的，这很有趣。

segments.en: So it's not really working.
segments.zh: 所以它真的不起作用。

segments.en: I guess we're going to have to find other ways to make people more conscious about this vice.
segments.zh: 我想我们将不得不找到其他方法来让人们对这个恶习更加有意识。

segments.en: Katerina We should.
segments.zh: 卡特琳娜 我们应该。

segments.en: Enrique But come to our website at EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: Enrique，但请访问我们的网站 englishpod.com。

segments.en: Tell us what you think about this vice, smoking.
segments.zh: 告诉我们你对这个恶习的看法，吸烟。

segments.en: Is it good?
segments.zh: 好吗？

segments.en: Is it bad?
segments.zh: 不好吗？

segments.en: Are you a habitual smoker or just a social smoker?
segments.zh: 您是习惯性吸烟者还是只是社交吸烟者？

segments.en: Katerina Yeah, we also have lots of great stuff, tools for you on our website and expansion sentences and all that stuff that helps you continue your studies outside of, well, the car or your house.
segments.zh: Katerina 是的，我们在我们的网站和扩展句子上也有很多很棒的东西，工具和所有可以帮助你在汽车或你的房子之外继续学习的东西。

segments.en: So check it out.
segments.zh: 那么来看看。

segments.en: Let us know what you think.
segments.zh: 让我们知道您的想法。

segments.en: And until next time.
segments.zh: 那么，下次见。

segments.en: Enrique All right, we'll see you there.
segments.zh: 恩里克 好的，我们会在那里见到你。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
